questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most important aspects for me were the university's ranking and its location.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I received all relevant information before my arrival. NYU's website has a lot of information in relation to anything you may need to know for the start of your semester like registering for courses, finding accommodation etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I stayed at the university's residence halls which have a 24/7 reception desk. They were very helpful upon my arrival. The first 2 weeks at university, I attended a summer course “Introduction to U.S. Law and Practice” before the start of the Fall semester. It was very insightful because, in addition to the substantive material on U.S. law, it contained a lot of practical information on studying in the U.S. such as how to find and read U.S. cases, how to use the relevant legal databases etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Shared apartments with 1 or 2 other students. Studio apartments if you prefer living alone.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There is a meal plan for a fixed fee per semester. However, there are a lot of nice and cheap restaurants in the area, so I would not recommend the meal plan at university. One tip is to check for lunch offers at the restaurants in the area. There is a really good Thai place nearby and an Italian restaurant called Piccola Cuccina with a good lunch offer.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a great way of meeting people and making friends from the start of the semester. The rooms are spacious and furnished with everything you need. However, you have to buy your own sheets, pillows, duvet, towels etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You get a free Amazon Prime account through NYU. You can get express free delivery, so one tip is to order everything you need for your room online before or upon your arrival.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The system is a bit confusing and it takes time to understand it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is a bidding system for courses. It is hard to say exactly how much you should bid on any particular course. It is most likely that a course that has been historically popular will continue to be popular. Some courses have a very limited number of places available, e.g., 20 so I would suggest bidding most of your points on them. There are courses which are very large and everyone who is interested, gets them, so there is no need to bid on them. If you cannot get a course that you really want, you can always try to e-mail the professor and ask directly if you can sign up. It is possible for them to make an exception (cannot rely on it though).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: NYU has a very helpful webpage with tutorial videos on the bidding process. In addition, you can always e-mail NYU to ask if you have any specific questions. I would also suggest joining the LLM WhatsApp groups because people often discuss it and it is a nice way to keep up with the process, deadlines etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the courses I wanted except one (which was a very small course for only 8 people). I changed my preferences a few times and did not experience any problems with dropping/re-registering for courses, so overall it was easy to get the courses I want.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bid most, if not all of your points, on the course that is the hardest to get in. For example, I bid all 1000 points on the Antitrust Law and Economics Seminar which was very popular and had limited number of spaces. The rest of my courses had a big intake to I got them “for free” without having to use any of my points for them. Another advice is to join the LLM WhatsApp group as the discussions there can be helpful in relation to determining your strategy for bidding and being on top of all daily bidding deadlines.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In my experience, the level is higher than the courses at UCPH. There is no “maximum” pages of assigned readings, as it is the case at UCPH. So, for some of the courses you may have more than 200 pages of reading per week.  The exams are normally more time pressured than the exams at UCPH. The exam questions are also much harder. However, this should not discourage you because the lowest grade that seems to be given to exchange students is a B or worst case, B-. So even you find a course very challenging, this is unlikely to be reflected in your grades.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The teaching style is more interactive compared to UCPH. A lot of the courses include practical exercises such as practicing drafting or negotiating, which can be very fun and insightful. In general, most courses are aimed at making you a better lawyer in a certain field, so they are not focused purely on the theoretical aspects but also aim to give you insights into the real world and enhance your interpersonal skills. 

In addition, in the U.S. you are expected to prepare and participate in every class. A lot of professors apply the “Socratic” method of teaching where they call on people to answer questions in class.  You are not “penalized” in any way if you are not prepared and cannot answer the question. However, it you are well-prepared and participate in classes, professors will normally bump up your grade. For example, if you receive B+ on the exam, if you have been participating in class, the professor is likely to give you A- as a final grade for the course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Corporations, Corporate Finance, Cross-border M&A, Antitrust Law and Economics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed and would recommend all of my courses. In general, I would recommend choosing courses relevant to the area of law that you would like to practice in your future career. It is very interesting to get the U.S. perspective and I think it can really advance your career if you want to work for international clients.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not have any unexpected costs, but some things were more expensive than I anticipated (see the answer below).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The compulsory health insurance is way more expensive (around $2,000 per semester). Mobile phone plan + data was more expensive (around $30 per month). Rent is way more expensive than in Copenhagen. Groceries (if you shop at Trader Joe's) are cheaper than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a free gym and sport center, discounted tickets for movie theaters and Broadway shows.  At university, there are a lot of very interesting lectures and academic events with famous guest speakers.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I did not participate in any non-academic activities because I wanted to use my free time exploring the city. However, you can find an overview of the different opportunities on the NYU website. For example, see
https://www.law.nyu.edu/graduateaffairs/academics/cocurricular
,
https://www.law.nyu.edu/studentgroups

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend exploring the city and everything it has to offer such as museums, art galleries, Broadway shows, comedy shows, restaurants etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: People are very friendly and open, which makes it easy to adjust to the local culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The best way to meet local students is in class but in general most international students stick together and it is easier to make friends within the international group. In general, American students were very friendly and open so you shouldn't hesitate to approach them and introduce yourself if you're interested in getting to know someone. There is a large international community with people from all around the world if you struggle making friends with the locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated American people's openness and friendliness. It was very easy to make friends and build a network which I found very rewarding.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. If you are used to being one of the best students in your class, this won't be the case when you go abroad, especially at NYU. The earlier you realize and embrace it, the more enjoyable your academic experience will be. It is not worth being stressed out and overworking yourself to try to catch up and compete with the others. Most people there will have better understanding of common law and how to do well at a U.S. university. In addition, most people come with a few years of working experience before starting their law degree. So, try to learn from them and accept that probably you will be one of the least experienced people in class.  

2. The best way to study and prepare for exams is by using outlines from previous students. They are shared in WhatsApp groups and some of them can be found on the university's website. If you can't find any, just ask the other students. The outlines are normally very comprehensive, so it is a waste of time making your own notes from scratch. 

3. You should not worry too much about exams and grades whilst you are on exchange. The most important thing is to get to know and experience another culture and a different way of living. You will make memories for life, so you don't want to spend most of your time in the library.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Getting a Revolut bank account is a good way to exchange money and save on bank fees whilst you are abroad.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all around the world and making new friends in addition to experiencing American culture and living in NYC as a local.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was managing my time between studying/preparing for classes and social activities outside campus as NYC has so much to offer.

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
